findings.quote: Forgetting that F and the weight pass through C (so they cannot be left out of the torque count as if they contributed) leads to setting up the wrong torque equation.
findings.note: The parenthetical states the opposite of the fact it is trying to teach: F and the weight pass through C, so their torque about C is zero and they are correctly left out of the torque equation. As written the entry tells the student they must be included.
findings.fix: Forgetting that F and the weight both pass through C, and so produce zero torque about C, leads to a wrong torque equation with extra terms in it.

notes: N = 40 N, f = 20 N, torque about C with h measured upward: 40h + 20(0.10) = 0 gives h = -0.05 m, i.e. 5 cm below C. All five equation lines are consistent with this. Mistake entry [1] correctly produces 0.10 m.
